headline: Bank of England Raises Benchmark Interest Rate to 4% to Combat Inflation
summary: The Bank of England raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point to 4%, marking its first rate increase since 2023. Policymakers cited lingering inflation pressures driven by high energy costs as the key driver for tightening borrowing costs.
why: Central bank interest rate decisions directly influence commercial borrowing costs, sovereign bond yields, and currency valuations, serving as a primary tool for managing macroeconomic inflation.

impacts.name: Bank of England Official Bank Rate
impacts.why: The central bank raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 4%.
